Title: Implement GaussianHMM.posterior().rsample()
Problem:
FR parallel-scan GaussianHMM.rsample()
`GaussianHMM.rsample()` would enable a powerful class of guides for time-series models with non-Gaussian likelihoods. Consider for example a guide:
```py
from pyro.distributions import GaussianHMM
from pyro.ops.gaussian import Gaussian

def model(data):
    p_z = GaussianHMM(*my_prior)  # prior, say a Matern GP
    z = pyro.sample("z", p_z)  # samples from prior
    p_x = dist.Normal(*noisy_nonlinear_function(z))
    pyro.sample("x", p_x, obs=data)  # likelihood

def guide(data):
    p_z = GaussianHMM(*my_prior)  # same as in the model
    p_x_given_z = Gaussian(*my_nn(data))  # independent over time
    p_z_given_x = forward_filter(p_z, p_x_given_z)  # updates trans_dist
    assert isinstance(p_z_given_x, GaussianHMM)  # posterior is still Gaussian
    pyro.sample("z", p_z_given_x)  # samples from posterior via GaussianHMM.rsample()
```
In this guide, `my_nn` acts as a weak encoder, forming a gaussian update `(log_normalizer, info_vec, precision)` independently at each time step, kind of a neural EP. In principle it is easy to fuse these weak likelihoods with a strong prior, e.g. a Matern GP, and then draw a posterior sample using parallel-scan.

This guide would work well with either continuous observations and `Trace_ELBO` loss, or discrete observations (e.g. `Poisson`) and a `Trace_CRPS` loss. I'd like to add this class of guides to `pyro.contrib.timeseries`.

Full disclosure, some of our users provide data that becomes wildly unbalanced, e.g., 2 values in one array and 17,000 in the other (see example code).
